root_cause.text: The -EBUSY error handling in tls_do_encryption() double-cleans encrypt_pending and scatterlist entries when tls_encrypt_async_wait() returns an error, because the async callback tls_encrypt_done() already performs the same cleanup, leading to corruption of the encrypt_pending sentinel and a subsequent use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explains: "When crypto_aead_encrypt() returns -EBUSY ... the async callback tls_encrypt_done() will be invoked ... That callback unconditionally restores the scatterlist entry ... and decrements ctx->encrypt_pending. However, if tls_encrypt_async_wait() returns an error, the synchronous error path in tls_do_encryption() performs the same cleanup again, double-decrementing encrypt_pending and double-restoring the scatterlist." The patch adds a check to skip the synchronous cleanup when the async wait returns an error, confirming this root cause.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix double cleanup when async encryption fails by returning early after the async callback has already cleaned up.
intent_record.what: Added an early return after a failed async encryption wait, removing the record from the list before the synchronous cleanup block.
intent_record.how: When tls_encrypt_async_wait returns an error (not -EINPROGRESS), the callback has already decremented encrypt_pending and restored sge. The new code deletes the record from the list and returns immediately, preventing duplicate cleanup.

grouping_result.intent: Fix double cleanup when async encryption fails by returning early after the async callback has already cleaned up.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly fixes the double cleanup issue described in the vulnerability root cause by returning early after the async callback has performed cleanup, preventing the subsequent double cleanup in the error path.

candidates.rationale: This condition allows the cleanup block to execute when tls_encrypt_async_wait() returns a non-zero error. Since the async callback already performed cleanup, entering this block causes double cleanup.

This atomic decrement of encrypt_pending is the direct double-cleanup action. The async callback tls_encrypt_done() already decrements it, so this second decrement corrupts the sentinel and leads to use-after-free.

bic_trace_step.reason: The code in this commit defines tls_do_encryption() and tls_encrypt_done() without the double-cleanup pattern: for async (-EINPROGRESS), tls_do_encryption does not adjust sg or free resources, leaving cleanup solely to the callback; for sync (rc==0), it handles sg adjustment and then proceeds to transmit, with no callback invoked. The vulnerable double-cleanup described (involving tls_encrypt_async_wait) is not present. Therefore the vulnerable construct is absent.

The root cause describes a double-clean when tls_encrypt_async_wait() returns an error, but that function does not exist in this commit.
